common_name: Knock 'em Red Coneflower (Color Coded Series Echinacea)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring after frost danger passes, in well-drained soil in full sun; this compact Color Coded series selection was bred by Walters Gardens for strong basal branching and consistent bloom color.

directions: Knock 'em Red is a compact, heavily branched coneflower that opens deep crimson and matures to a bright, fluorescent red as the four-inch blooms age. Plant in average to lean, well-drained soil; once established it tolerates heat and drought with minimal care. Deadheading encourages continued flowering, while leaving late-season seed heads intact provides food for finches and other birds. Its dense habit and uniform height make it well suited to mass plantings and mid-border pollinator plantings.
sources: Proven Winners plant catalog, Color Coded series

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained garden soil in full to part sun; this Walters Gardens introduction was selected for its large flower size and resistance to Septoria leaf spot, a common foliar disease of black-eyed Susans.

directions: Treasure Trove produces large, golden-yellow, star-shaped flowers with dark brown centers on well-branched stems from midsummer into fall. Its standout trait among modern black-eyed Susans is foliage that resists Septoria leaf spot, so plants kept their clean, full look through multiple years of grower trials without the early-season leaf drop common to older cultivars. Give it full sun and average, well-drained soil, and avoid overhead watering late in the day to further reduce fungal pressure. Established clumps are long-lived and draw bees, butterflies, and seed-eating birds through autumn.

common_name: Decadence Deluxe Lemon Smoothie Baptisia (Late-Blooming Yellow False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in full to part sun in average to lean, well-drained soil; a Decadence Deluxe series introduction from Walters Gardens hybridizer Hans Hansen, bred from native Baptisia species collected in Texas and Oklahoma.

directions: Lemon Smoothie sends up tall, strongly branched flower spikes packed with sunny yellow blooms that open noticeably later in the season than older yellow Baptisia such as Lemon Meringue, extending the false indigo bloom window. Once its deep taproot is established, the plant is heat and drought tolerant and shrugs off deer browsing. Site it where its large mature size can stay undisturbed, since Baptisia resents transplanting once mature. After flowering, the dark seed pods add textural interest and can be left standing for winter structure.
sources: Proven Winners plant catalog, Decadence Deluxe series, 2026 new variety listing
